overview: First Pacific is a Hong Kong-headquartered, Bermuda-incorporated investment holding company controlled by the Salim family (Chairman Anthoni Salim) that holds controlling or significant economic interests in a portfolio of Asia-Pacific operating companies spanning consumer food products (Indofood, Indonesia), telecommunications (PLDT, Philippines), infrastructure (MPIC, Philippines), power (FPM Power/Meralco, PacificLight Power in Singapore), and natural resources (Philex Mining and PXP Energy, Philippines). It does not operate businesses directly; it earns returns through its share of consolidated/associated-company profits, dividends and fees upstreamed from these investees, reporting results in USD while its shares trade in HKD on the HKEX (also available as US ADRs).

business_model.summary: First Pacific is a holding/investment company, not an operating business. It consolidates majority-owned subsidiaries (Indofood, MPIC) and equity-accounts for associates (PLDT, Philex), earning 'contribution from operations' (operating companies' recurring profit net of tax and non-controlling interests) plus dividend and fee income at the Head Office level, less Head Office overhead and net interest expense. Economic interests (as of early 2026): Indofood 50.1%, PLDT 25.6%, MPIC 49.9%, FPM Power Holdings 69.5% (incl. indirect Meralco interest), Philex 31.2% (plus an additional 15.0% via affiliate Two Rivers), PXP 29.3%. Reported/consolidated revenue is dominated by Indofood and MPIC; PLDT and Philex are equity-accounted associates whose revenue does not consolidate, only their profit contribution does.

revenue_streams.name: Indofood (consumer food products - Indonesia)
revenue_streams.note: Share of profit contribution from operations by sector; FY2025 Indofood contribution ~US$342.2m

revenue_streams.name: MPIC / infrastructure (Philippines - toll roads, water, power, rail, hospitals)
revenue_streams.note: FY2025 infrastructure contribution ~US$343.2m, driven by Maynilad water tariffs and MPTC toll roads

revenue_streams.name: PLDT / telecommunications (Philippines)
revenue_streams.note: FY2025 telecom contribution ~US$145.1m; equity-accounted associate, not consolidated revenue

revenue_streams.name: Natural resources (Philex, PXP - mining, oil & gas)
revenue_streams.note: Small today but Silangan copper-gold project targeted to start contributing from 2026

revenue_streams.name: Singapore power (FPM Power / PacificLight Power)
revenue_streams.note: Included within infrastructure/other in some disclosures; contribution softened in H1 2026 on lower non-fuel margin

business_model.customer_type: Indirect - First Pacific's 'customers' are its own operating companies' end customers (consumers, telecom subscribers, toll-road/water/power users in Indonesia, Philippines and Singapore); First Pacific itself has no direct customer base, only shareholders/investors
business_model.geographic_mix: Philippines ~48-49% of profit contribution from operations, Indonesia ~41-42%, Singapore ~9-11%; Head Office based in Hong Kong with USD-denominated debt and reporting

main_competitors: Other Asian conglomerate/holding companies (e.g., Jardine Matheson, Swire Pacific, CK Hutchison) as capital-allocation comparables
Within Indofood's markets: Wilmar International, Mayora Indah, Nestle Indonesia (food/noodles)
Within PLDT's market: Globe Telecom (Philippines duopoly)
Within MPIC's infrastructure businesses: Ayala-linked infrastructure/water/power operators, San Miguel Corporation's toll road and power units
Within Philex/mining: OceanaGold, Nickel Asia and other Philippine miners
competitive_position.market_position: First Pacific's underlying investees generally hold #1 or #2 market positions in their respective niches (Indofood is Indonesia's largest vertically integrated food company and global leader in instant noodles via Indomie; PLDT is the dominant integrated telecom/broadband operator in the Philippines; MPIC's subsidiaries are the largest toll-road operator, largest water concessionaire (Maynilad) and largest power distributor (via Meralco) in their Philippine service areas). First Pacific itself, as a holding vehicle, has no operating market share - its position is as a capital allocator and control-stake holder.

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory/concession barriers at the operating-company level
moat_factors.description: MPIC's water, toll road and power distribution concessions and PLDT's telecom license/spectrum create high barriers to entry that First Pacific benefits from as a controlling shareholder

moat_factors.factor: Scale and brand in Indonesian food
moat_factors.description: Indofood/Indomie is a dominant, deeply entrenched consumer brand with vertically integrated supply chain (flour milling via Bogasari, plantations, distribution) that is difficult to replicate

moat_factors.factor: Long-standing control relationships and local market knowledge
moat_factors.description: Decades-long Salim family/First Pacific management relationships with Philippine (Pangilinan/MVP group) and Indonesian conglomerates provide deal flow and governance influence, but this is a people-dependent, not structural, advantage
Spreads single-country or single-sector risk, but this is also a source of complexity and conglomerate discount

weaknesses: First Pacific itself has no operating moat - it is purely a passive/semi-active capital allocator exposed to the execution of its investees' management teams

Persistent, large holding-company discount: share price traded at a 17-60% discount to adjusted NAV over 2016-2025 (17.2% at end-2025, improved sharply from 38-60% in prior years but still structurally present)

Complex multi-layer corporate and ownership structure (direct stakes, indirect stakes via Two Rivers, FPM Power/Meralco cross-holdings) makes the investment case hard for investors to evaluate and is a classic conglomerate-discount driver

Minority/non-controlling interest dilution - First Pacific often owns less than 100% (e.g., 50.1% Indofood, 25.6% PLDT, 49.9% MPIC), so a large share of subsidiary profit (NCI was US$1,119.9m in FY2025, nearly double First Pacific's own US$661.0m attributable profit) accrues to other shareholders
Concentration in two emerging-market currencies (Indonesian rupiah, Philippine peso) with limited hedging of translation exposure

growth_drivers: Maynilad Water IPO (November 2025, PHP 15/share, ~PHP34bn raised, Philippines' second-largest-ever listing) unlocked value and provided MPIC/First Pacific with capital and a quoted market valuation benchmark for its water business
Philex's Silangan copper-gold project in Mindanao expected to begin contributing profit from 2026, diversifying the natural resources segment beyond the maturing Padcal mine
PLDT's Maya fintech unit turned profitable in 2025 and is reportedly targeting a dual US/Philippines IPO in H2 2026, which could crystallize value in a high-growth, underbanked-market business
Continued toll-road and water tariff increases plus higher traffic/billed-volume growth at MPIC's Philippine infrastructure assets (MPTC, Maynilad)
New MPIC investment in PT Jasamarga Transjawa Tol (Indonesian toll road, acquired 2024) extends the infrastructure platform into Indonesia
PLP (PacificLight Power, Singapore) capacity expansion - new 100MW fast-start plant delivered on time/budget and a S$1.2bn 670MW H-class CCGT plant under contract for 2029 online date
Progressive/record-high ordinary dividend policy (six consecutive years of double-digit recurring profit growth through FY2025) with potential for continued re-rating as the NAV discount narrows
Secular tailwinds in emerging Southeast Asia: rising middle-class food consumption in Indonesia, continued telecom/data and infrastructure buildout in the Philippines

business.description: First Pacific's results depend entirely on the operating and capital-allocation decisions of Indofood, PLDT, MPIC and Philex management teams, over which First Pacific has influence but not full day-to-day control (especially PLDT and Philex, which are associates)
Multi-layer ownership (direct, indirect via Two Rivers, FPM Power/Meralco) makes valuation and governance oversight difficult
Indofood's plantation (CPO) business and Philex's gold/copper output expose First Pacific's profit to volatile commodity prices

Significant continuing connected transactions between Indofood Group entities and Salim-family-affiliated distributors (e.g., SBTC US$278m, TJTI US$36m in FY2025) raise related-party governance considerations, even though reviewed by INEDs and auditors

financial.description: Group net debt US$8.74bn vs total equity US$13.1bn (gearing 0.67x) at FY2025; MPIC alone carries ~0.98x gearing and PLDT (associate) 2.21x; Head Office leverage 1.41x against its own equity

Group NAV and earnings are heavily exposed to the Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso; a 1% adverse move in rupiah/peso reduces adjusted NAV by an estimated US$48.2m (8.84 HK cents/share); H1 2026 recurring profit fell 3% partly due to 5.6% peso and 4.9% rupiah depreciation; ICBP's USD-denominated bonds generate non-cash FX losses on rupiah weakness

Group carries large long-term borrowings (consolidated total borrowings US$13.0bn); Head Office refinanced its only near-term maturity in Jan 2026, leaving no further maturities until Sept 2027, but subsidiaries (MPIC, Indofood, PLP) continue to raise new debt for capex and investments
Roxas Holdings' (sugar) borrowings were reclassified as current due to covenant compliance issues at year-end 2025

regulatory.description: Philippine telecom/infrastructure/water tariff regulation (NTC, MWSS, toll road regulators, ERC for power) and Indonesian food/agribusiness and foreign-investment rules can directly affect investee profitability and dividend upstreaming
Extensive web of continuing connected transactions with Salim-family-affiliated entities requires ongoing Listing Rule Chapter 14A compliance, annual INED review and auditor confirmation
Reliance on dividends and fees upstreamed from Indonesian and Philippine subsidiaries to service Head Office debt and fund shareholder distributions

macro.description: Earnings and NAV are directly geared to IDR and PHP strength/weakness and to Philippine/Indonesian interest rates, which drive MPIC's and PLDT's high finance costs
Management explicitly cited 'turbulent geopolitical and geoeconomic headwinds' in the FY2025 Chairman's letter as a risk to the medium-term outlook
Crude palm oil prices affect Indofood's plantation segment; gold/copper prices affect Philex and the upcoming Silangan project economics

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Diversified exposure to Southeast Asian consumer staples, telecom/digital services, and infrastructure - sectors generally viewed as benefiting from continued urbanization, rising middle-class consumption, and infrastructure under-investment in Indonesia and the Philippines; management expressed 'guarded and positive optimism' for 2026 and beyond
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - consumer food (Indofood) is relatively defensive, while infrastructure usage (toll traffic, power demand) has some macro sensitivity and mining/plantation segments are more cyclical/commodity-driven
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - Group interest cover of ~5.1x and consolidated gearing of 0.67x (with PLDT and MPIC associates carrying higher leverage) make net profit sensitive to Philippine and Indonesian benchmark rates and USD funding costs
key_input_costs: Raw materials/wheat and palm oil costs for Indofood
Fuel costs for PLP's gas-fired power generation
Construction/capex costs for MPIC's toll road, water and rail concessions
Equipment and development costs for Philex's Silangan project

recent_developments.event: Maynilad Water Services IPO on the Philippine Stock Exchange (ticker MYNLD) priced at PHP15/share, raising ~PHP34.3bn and becoming the second-largest IPO in PSE history; First Pacific's effective interest in Maynilad diluted to 38.6% from 53.7%; share price reportedly rose over a third in the months after listing

FY2025 annual results: record recurring profit of US$740.0m (+10%) and record reported profit of US$661.0m (+10%); sixth consecutive year of double-digit recurring profit growth; adjusted NAV discount narrowed to 17.2% from 38.2% a year earlier; total distribution of 28.15 HK cents/share (21% payout ratio)
Renewal of multiple continuing connected transactions within the Indofood Group (plantations, distribution, flour, noodles, insurance, dairy, packaging) with new annual caps set for 2026-2028

Philex reported a Q1 2026 net income of PHP392m (more than doubling) and sustained Padcal operations after crusher repairs; Silangan copper-gold project described as nearing commissioning, targeted for 2026 start, though not yet confirmed as producing as of July 2026

H1 2026 results: turnover up 6% to US$5.3bn, but recurring profit down 3% to US$365.9m and reported profit down 23% to US$301.5m, driven by 5.6% peso and 4.9% rupiah average depreciation (at constant FX, recurring profit would have been +3%) and a non-cash FX loss on ICBP's USD bonds; interim distribution of 1.67 US cents/share declared
PLDT's fintech associate Maya reportedly planning a dual US/Philippines IPO in H2 2026 after turning profitable in 2025; PLDT/First Pacific combined stake in Maya ~39-40%
Citi reiterated Buy with HK$7.30 price target; CLSA Buy with HK$8.20 target (late 2025); consensus analyst rating 'Strong Buy' per Investing.com aggregation

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (August 2026) and FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026)

items.notes: Chairman's letter (March 2026) expressed 'guarded and positive optimism' amid 'turbulent geopolitical and geoeconomic headwinds'; CEO's letter cited an 'optimistic' outlook for continuing earnings growth, highlighting MPIC and Indofood as lead contributors and Silangan as a new 2026 profit contributor

items.vs_prior: new - first guidance of a contribution date
items.notes: Philex's Silangan copper-gold project in Mindanao; as of mid-2026 reporting it was nearing but had not confirmed commissioning
Expands PacificLight Power's Singapore generation capacity

items.vs_prior: maintained - consistent with historical 20-28% payout range
items.notes: Management reiterated the 'progressive dividend policy' intent to keep raising per-share distributions as profits grow

items.target: H1 2026 recurring profit would have been +3% at constant FX vs reported -3%
items.vs_prior: disclosure added to explain FX drag
items.notes: Management flagged peso (-5.6%) and rupiah (-4.9%) average depreciation as the main driver of the reported decline, implying underlying operating momentum remains positive

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Anthoni Salim (FY2025 letter): 'Notwithstanding economic headwinds borne by uncertainties beyond our markets, we remain confident that the expectations of strong, medium-term economic growth in our markets form a strong basis for a positive outlook for First Pacific... we look ahead with guarded and positive optimism.' CEO Manuel V. Pangilinan: 'In our financial year 2025, First Pacific recorded its sixth year in a row of double-digit growth in recurring profit... The overall operational outlook is promising, and we are optimistic about continuing earnings growth in the years ahead,' citing MPIC and Indofood as lead drivers, PLDT's Home broadband growth and Maya's fintech turnaround, and Silangan's expected 2026 profit contribution as the mine nears launch.

bull_case: Trading at a meaningful discount to adjusted NAV (17.2% at end-FY2025, though narrowed sharply from 38-60% in prior years) offers potential re-rating upside as portfolio companies' intrinsic values are increasingly crystallized via events like the Maynilad IPO

Six consecutive years of double-digit recurring profit growth and record dividends demonstrate durable earnings power across a diversified, defensively-positioned portfolio of market-leading Southeast Asian businesses

Multiple embedded value-unlocking catalysts: Maynilad already listed (Nov 2025), Maya fintech targeting a dual-market IPO in H2 2026, and Silangan copper-gold mine starting to contribute profit from 2026

Exposure to structurally growing Southeast Asian consumer, telecom/digital and infrastructure demand (Indonesia and Philippines) via controlling or influential stakes in category leaders (Indomie/Indofood, PLDT, Maynilad, MPTC, Meralco)
Progressive dividend policy with strong distribution cover (4.8x in FY2025) provides a visible, growing income stream even if the NAV discount persists
bear_case: Persistent holding-company/conglomerate discount structure means NAV growth does not reliably translate into share price performance, and the discount could widen again as it has historically (ranged 17-66% over the past decade)

High leverage throughout the group (consolidated gearing 0.67x, MPIC ~0.98x, PLDT associate 2.21x, Head Office 1.41x) leaves consolidated profit sensitive to rising rates and refinancing conditions in the Philippines and Indonesia

Heavy, largely unhedged exposure to Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso translation and transaction risk directly hit H1 2026 results (recurring profit -3%, reported profit -23%) despite healthy underlying operating performance

Complex multi-layer ownership structure (direct stakes, Two Rivers indirect interests, FPM Power/Meralco cross-holding, extensive related-party transactions with Salim-family affiliates) makes the investment thesis difficult to evaluate and perpetuates governance/transparency concerns
Growth catalysts (Silangan mine ramp-up, Maya IPO timing, PLP's 2029 plant) carry meaningful execution and timing risk and are not yet reflected in current earnings
